packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Codex isolated image-only reader (model version not exposed)
text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 08

Inputs: PROMPT.md, packet.json, image-001.jpg and image-002.jpg only. No identification, catalogue, edition, or earlier transcription was consulted; no proposed identification was exposed.

Layout survey
Both images are upright as supplied. Each shows a severely damaged, stained, abraded leaf with irregular edge losses and holes. Brown cursive writing occupies a broad vertical field; I cannot securely resolve a two-column arrangement. The images seem to show opposite sides of the same physical object, judging only by the mirrored holes and edge contour; they are not overlapping text crops. On image-002, a thin vertical boundary is visible to the left of the clearest upper writing. No secure running title, rubric, enlarged initial, underlining, or separate marginal/interlinear gloss can be distinguished. In particular, faint intersecting marks cannot reliably be separated from abrasion or show-through. No main-text/commentary distinction is justified.

Selected spans
The upper third is appreciably clearer than the rest. There is no securely legible heading or question opening. I attempted two short samples there, but cannot recover two continuous useful passages. The fragments below should not be used as established readings or completed from grammar.

Physical line labels count apparent text baselines from the top of each ORIGINAL image. Because the first lines are faint, these ordinal counts are approximate; original pixel positions make the selected lines unambiguous. Each original is 4512 × 6530 pixels.

Sample A, image-001.jpg, upper text:
image-001.jpg L7? (baseline approximately y=1350): [illegible] et sic? mollis? et [illegible]
image-001.jpg L8? (baseline approximately y=1470): [illegible] dicat̄? [illegible]
image-001.jpg L9? (baseline approximately y=1590): [illegible]

Sample B, image-002.jpg, upper text:
image-002.jpg L7? (baseline approximately y=1390): pluvie? [illegible]
image-002.jpg L8? (baseline approximately y=1510): pluvie? [illegible] q̄libet? [illegible]
image-002.jpg L9? (baseline approximately y=1620): [illegible] nos? facit? [illegible]

These are uncertain visual letter-group reports, not a recovered sentence. Even the repeated initial group in Sample B may have been misread. Abbreviation strokes are present, but no confident expansions are proposed. I cannot identify a visible deletion or addition with confidence.

Inspection/transforms
Viewed both complete supplied images. Made unmodified pixel crops for each image at (902,457)–(3880,1828), then image-001 at (950,1200)–(3150,1650) and image-002 at (1400,1240)–(3500,1650), with coordinates measured from original top left. Inspected detail crops at native scale. No rotation, contrast enhancement, sharpening, or generated restoration. These crops repeat the same physical lines; they add no new text.

Limitations and unread areas
Nearly all lower and outer writing remains unread, as do the faint upper beginnings and endings of the selected lines. Surface loss, mottling and fading prevent a responsible continuous transcription from these photographs. A different-light or multispectral photograph would be more useful than further enlargement. Wider views are already supplied; adjacent crops alone cannot restore lost ink.
